rules.statement: Put a submitted delivery in `deliveries/<slug>/` with a `delivery.json` whose `delivery.id` equals the slug and whose `submission` object states the title, the submitter handle, the licence, the profile used, the tool versions and the attestation.
rules.rationale: Reviewers and the intake tool find a delivery by its folder and its manifest, and a handle ties it to its author.

how_to_check.method: automated: the finding carries rule id X-70

examples.bad: deliveries/My Study/ with no submission object

rules.statement: Offer the delivery under a licence the profile lists (`submission.allowedLicences`; by default CC BY 4.0, or CC0 when the delivery says so).
rules.rationale: A catalogue entry must carry uniform, known terms for everyone who uses it later.

how_to_check.method: automated: the finding carries rule id X-71

rules.fix_hint: Set submission.licence to one of the licences the profile lists (CC-BY-4.0 or CC0-1.0 by default) and make the provenance entries agree.

rules.statement: Include only files of the types the profile lists (`submission.allowedExtensions`; by default ifc, glb, png, jpg, json, md, csv and txt), with no program, script or archive and no executable file mode.
rules.rationale: A delivery is data; anything that can run or unpack itself is a risk to every person and tool that opens it.

how_to_check.method: automated: the finding carries rule id X-72

rules.fix_hint: Remove the file, or convert the content to a listed type (ifc, glb, png, jpg, json, md, csv, txt); clear the executable bit with chmod -x.

rules.statement: Keep a delivery within the profile's limits: at most `submission.maxFiles` files (200), `submission.maxFileBytes` per file (25 MiB) and `submission.maxDeliveryBytes` in total (100 MiB).
rules.rationale: Review and intake run on shared machines with fixed time and memory.

how_to_check.method: automated: the finding carries rule id X-73

rules.fix_hint: Remove files that are not needed, reduce texture sizes or geometry, or split the delivery into two deliveries.

examples.bad: 900 files or a single 80 MB texture

rules.statement: Use only relative, portable paths: no leading slash, no `..`, no backslash or drive letter, names of letters, digits, dot, hyphen and underscore that do not start with a dot, no reserved device names, no two names that differ only by case, and no path longer than `submission.maxPathLength`, in the folder and in every path the manifest and the checksum list name.
rules.rationale: A path that leaves the delivery folder or collides on another system can overwrite or hide a file.

how_to_check.method: automated: the finding carries rule id X-74

rules.fix_hint: Rename the file to letters, digits, dot, hyphen and underscore, without a leading dot, and make every path in delivery.json and SHA256SUMS.txt relative with forward slashes.

rules.statement: Include no symbolic link and no special file, only plain files and folders.
rules.rationale: A link can point outside the delivery and make a reader open a file that was never submitted.

how_to_check.method: automated: the finding carries rule id X-75

rules.fix_hint: Replace the link by a copy of the file it points to.

rules.statement: Have the submitter attest in `submission.attestation` that the work is their own or they may offer it, that they may license it under the stated licence, and that it holds no restricted third-party content.
rules.rationale: The maintainers cannot check ownership, so the statement is on record with the delivery.

how_to_check.method: automated: the finding carries rule id X-76

rules.fix_hint: Set the three attestation fields to true only if they are true, otherwise do not submit the delivery.

examples.good: ownWork, mayLicense and noRestrictedContent all true

rules.statement: Make every file what its name says: PNG and JPEG images that are real images within `submission.maxImagePixels`, GLB files that are binary glTF 2 of the stated length, IFC files that are IFC text files, JSON that parses, text in UTF-8 without NUL bytes or active markup (script, iframe, object, embed).
rules.rationale: A renamed file can hide content from review and can crash a reader.

how_to_check.method: automated: the finding carries rule id X-77

rules.fix_hint: Re-export the file in the type its name says, within the pixel limit, or rename it to its real type if that is allowed.

examples.good: a PNG with a PNG header

rules.statement: Put a proof manifest at `proofs/manifest.json` (format `proofs/1`) that lists every GLB, the GLB validation report and every render with its SHA-256, size and the tool and version that made it, and put nothing else in `proofs/`.
rules.rationale: One file must say exactly which models and pictures belong to which source, so that a change after the fact is visible.

how_to_check.method: automated: the finding carries rule id X-79

rules.fix_hint: Run python3 tools/build_proofs.py deliveries/SLUG; it writes proofs/manifest.json and everything it lists. Delete files in proofs/ that it did not write.

examples.good: proofs/manifest.json lists 6 GLB files, a report and 14 renders, each with its hash

rules.statement: Make every delivered GLB a valid binary glTF 2 file in metres with Y up, with no external reference, no unused buffer, image or material, finite and unit-length normals, tangents where a normal map is used, named scene-graph nodes, and the node, triangle and texture limits of the profile.
rules.rationale: A GLB that is malformed, in another unit or axis, or that points outside itself shows consumers a different building than the IFC file or crashes them.

how_to_check.method: automated: the finding carries rule id X-80

rules.fix_hint: Re-export with python3 tools/export_glb.py (do not edit GLB files by hand), then run python3 tools/validate_glb.py on them and fix what it names; each finding carries a code and a hint.

examples.good: a GLB in metres, Y up, every buffer used, unit normals
examples.bad: a GLB whose image is a file name, or whose triangles exceed limits.maxTriangles

rules.statement: Deliver a GLB of the whole master model and one of every item, covering, fixture, hardware piece, door, window and texture set, each made from the delivered IFC files (their SHA-256 is recorded), together with a validation report that passes and names every GLB by its SHA-256.
rules.rationale: The GLB files are what the pictures are made from and what a consumer without an IFC reader opens; they must correspond to the delivered source and be known to be valid.

how_to_check.method: automated: the finding carries rule id X-81

rules.fix_hint: Run python3 tools/build_proofs.py deliveries/SLUG after the last change to any IFC file, texture set or item; it regenerates the GLB files and the validation report together.

examples.good: one GLB per item, covering, fixture, door, window and texture set, plus model.glb, and a passing report
examples.bad: a new chair added to the IFC file but no GLB for it

rules.statement: Include renders that cover every level (a plan), every room kind present (the profile's number of interior views), the outside of the building, and every item, covering, fixture, hardware piece, door, window and texture set (a contact sheet).
rules.rationale: A picture set that leaves out a level, a kind of room or a component lets a defect there go unseen.

how_to_check.method: automated: the finding carries rule id X-82

rules.fix_hint: Run python3 tools/build_proofs.py deliveries/SLUG; it renders the standard set. A room needs a Function property so that its kind is known.

examples.good: a plan for every level, four views of each room kind, four exterior views, a sheet per component
examples.bad: a second level with no plan

rules.statement: Make every render from a GLB of the delivery and record in the manifest the SHA-256 of that GLB, of the picture itself, its pixel size, the camera and the lighting; each recorded GLB hash must be the hash of the delivered GLB file.
rules.rationale: A picture that cannot be traced to the exact model it shows proves nothing about it.

how_to_check.method: automated: the finding carries rule id X-83

rules.fix_hint: Re-render with python3 tools/build_proofs.py deliveries/SLUG; do not rename, resize or edit the pictures afterwards.

examples.good: a render whose glb hash is the hash of proofs/glb/model.glb
examples.bad: a render made from an earlier version of the model

rules.statement: Keep every render within the profile's pixel and file-size limits (`proofs.minRenderWidth`, `proofs.maxRenderPixels`, `proofs.maxRenderBytes`) and the whole `proofs/` folder within `proofs.maxProofBytes`.
rules.rationale: Pictures are for looking at on shared machines: a very large one costs every reviewer and a tiny one shows nothing.

how_to_check.method: automated: the finding carries rule id X-84

rules.fix_hint: Use the default sizes of tools/render.py; lower --scale only within the profile's minimum and raise nothing above its maximum.

rules.statement: Keep personal data and local paths out of images and GLB files: renders hold only the image chunks the profile allows, no image holds EXIF, XMP, a colour profile with text or text that names a person, a folder, a host or an address, and no GLB holds a path, an address, an e-mail address or a generator other than the set's.
rules.rationale: A file that records who made it, where or on which machine leaks that to everyone who receives the delivery.

how_to_check.method: automated: the finding carries rule id X-85

rules.fix_hint: Rebuild the proofs with tools/build_proofs.py, which writes images and GLB files without metadata. For your own pictures, re-save them without EXIF, XMP or text chunks.

examples.good: a PNG with only IHDR, IDAT and IEND chunks
examples.bad: a PNG with a tEXt chunk naming a folder on someone's disk

rules.statement: Make the proofs reproducible: rebuilding the GLB files from the delivered IFC files must give the same bytes, and re-rendering the delivered GLB files must give pictures that differ from the delivered ones by no more than `proofs.renderTolerance`; where the toolchain is not available the check says so and is skipped, not passed.
rules.rationale: Proofs that cannot be reproduced cannot be trusted, and a rebuild is the cheapest way to see that the pictures show the model.

how_to_check.method: automated: the finding carries rule id X-86

rules.fix_hint: Run python3 tools/check_proofs.py deliveries/SLUG --reproduce with the pinned requirements (tools/requirements-ci.txt); if the GLB bytes differ, rebuild the proofs with that toolchain.

examples.good: the rebuilt GLB files are byte-identical and every re-render is within tolerance
examples.bad: a render edited after it was made
